title.narrative: Increased capacities of national constituents to stimulate enterprise development for job creation including improving working conditions

description.narrative: In the Ten Years Perspective Plan of Ethiopia, 2021-2030, private sector development is included as one of the key elements towards macroeconomic performance. It identifies the need to address bottlenecks related to productivity, quality and competitiveness as critical for the private sector to contribute to sustainable development. The agriculture and manufacturing industry sectors are set forward as priorities for productivity improvements. The Plan of Action for Job Creation 2020-2025 includes two out of six strategic objectives that are linked to enterprise development. Firstly, building a vibrant local private sector by revamping the support to MSMEs and secondly, realizing the job-creation potential of prospective high-yield sectors including agriculture (horticulture) and industry (Agro processing, textile and apparel, renewable energy, etc.) The main objective of the CPO ETH28 is to respond to the above-mentioned plan of the Government of Ethiopia to crate decent jobs to men and women in the priority sectors identified. To this effect, the ILO through the ProAgro interventions will support job creation efforts of the Government by working in three sectors, namely of poultry, food and vegetables and edible oils to promote private sector and facilitate business models that enable job creation, enterprise development and skills development. This initiative is executed in close collaboration with UNIDO and GIZ. The activities are backstopped by the SME, Cooperatives, MNE and Social Finance units as well as the DWT-Cairo. Similarly, through the ONE ILO Programme, Advancing Decent Work and Inclusive Industrialization in the Garment and Textile Industry Programme, the ILO through this CPO works to improve working conditions, industrial relations and productivity in the key prioritized manufacturing sectors. At the factory level the work on enterprise productivity in the textile industry is carried out through the implementation of the SCORE programme.
